```yaml
    - Doctor partnerships with that country's clinics
    - Medical tourism agency contracts

phase_3_year_2_plus (2027+):
  long_tail_languages:
    ar: Arabic (RTL) — Middle East medical tourism
    fr: French — francophone Africa + tourism
    es: Spanish — Spanish-speaking tourism
  
  conditional_activation: case-by-case business need

total_capacity: 8 languages designed in architecture
implementation_order: Thai → English → others (just-in-time)
```

### 28.1.2 Why This Matters Architecturally

```yaml
multilingual_is_NOT:
  ❌ "Translate content at the end before publishing"
  ❌ "Same English content translated to other languages"
  ❌ "Add language switcher and call it done"

multilingual_IS:
  ✅ Cross-cutting architectural concern affecting:
     - Database schema (jsonb fields per language)
     - Entity model (single entity, multilingual labels)
     - Scoring system (per-language scores)
     - Schema markup (inLanguage, sameAs)
     - Translation workflow (AI-draft + review)
     - URL structure (subdirectory pattern)
     - WPML configuration (CPT translation rules)
     - Elementor templates (Dynamic Tags pull translated values)
     - DataForSEO tracking (per-locale data)
     - AI/LLMO strategy (multilingual citables)
     - Cross-brand referrals (language-aware)
```

## 28.2 URL Structure (Subdirectory + Thai Default)

### 28.2.1 Confirmed Decision

```yaml
url_pattern_locked:
  
  thai_default:
    homepage: vth-biodent.com/
    knowledge: vth-biodent.com/knowledge/peri-implantitis/
    procedure: vth-biodent.com/procedures/dental-implant/
    doctor: vth-biodent.com/doctors/dr-somchai/
  
  english:
    homepage: vth-biodent.com/en/
    knowledge: vth-biodent.com/en/knowledge/peri-implantitis/
    procedure: vth-biodent.com/en/procedures/dental-implant/
    doctor: vth-biodent.com/en/doctors/dr-somchai/
  
  future_languages:
    chinese: vth-biodent.com/zh/...
    japanese: vth-biodent.com/ja/...
    korean: vth-biodent.com/ko/...
    arabic: vth-biodent.com/ar/...    # RTL
    french: vth-biodent.com/fr/...
    spanish: vth-biodent.com/es/...

rationale_for_subdirectory:
  ✅ Single domain = cumulative authority
  ✅ Easier to manage SSL, CDN, analytics
  ✅ Simpler GSC setup (1 property)
  ✅ Clear hierarchy for users + crawlers
  ✅ WPML default + recommended pattern

rejected_alternatives:
  ❌ Subdomain (th.brand.com): splits authority
  ❌ Separate ccTLD (.co.th + .com): expensive, complex
  ❌ Query parameter (?lang=en): poor SEO
```

### 28.2.2 WPML Configuration

```yaml
wpml_settings:
  language_url_format: 'directory'    # /en/, /zh/ etc.
  default_language: 'th'              # Thai = no prefix
  default_url: 'no_prefix'             # /knowledge/ NOT /th/knowledge/
  
  language_negotiation_type: 1         # different languages in directories
  
  hidden_languages: []                # all visible
  
  url_normalization:
    case: lowercase
    trailing_slash: yes
    no_double_slashes: enforced
```

### 28.2.3 Special URL Cases

```yaml
non_translated_urls:
  
  signature_systems_(brand_specific):
    Thai default: vth-biodent.com/mbm/
    English: vth-biodent.com/en/mbm/
    
    Note: Branded methodologies (e.g., Mouth Bio Mapping)
          keep same slug across languages — name is universal
  
  doctor_profiles:
    Thai: vth-biodent.com/doctors/dr-somchai/
    English: vth-biodent.com/en/doctors/dr-somchai/
    
    Note: Doctor names slug = transliteration, kept same
          Display name varies (Dr. Somchai / นพ. สมชาย)

  branch_pages:
    Same slug across languages (location identifier)
    Display content fully translated
```

## 28.3 Entity Multilingual Pattern

### 28.3.1 Single Entity, Multilingual Labels

```yaml
core_decision:
  pattern: ONE entity record, multilingual values via jsonb
  
  not_used:
    ❌ Separate entity per language
    ❌ Translation tables joined to entity

rationale:
  ✅ Knowledge graph stays unified (1 entity = 1 concept)
  ✅ Edges defined once (not duplicated per language)
  ✅ Wikidata mapping cleaner (1 Q-ID per entity)
  ✅ ICD-10 / SNOMED codes universal (no duplication)
  ✅ Scoring computed at entity level (cross-language signals)
  ✅ AI/LLMO benefits from multilingual labels on same entity
```

### 28.3.2 Schema Implementation

```sql
-- Extends seo_entity_graph for multilingual

ALTER TABLE seo_entity_graph ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS
  canonical_names jsonb DEFAULT '{}';
-- Structure (per language ISO code):
-- {
--   "th": "โรคข้อต่อขากรรไกร",
--   "en": "Temporomandibular Joint Disorder",
--   "zh": "颞下颌关节紊乱",
--   "ja": "顎関節症",
--   "ko": "턱관절 장애",
--   "ar": "اضطراب المفصل الفكي الصدغي",
--   "fr": "Trouble de l'articulation temporo-mandibulaire",
--   "es": "Trastorno de la articulación temporomandibular"
-- }

ALTER TABLE seo_entity_graph ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS
  descriptions jsonb DEFAULT '{}';
-- Same per-language structure for description text

ALTER TABLE seo_entity_graph ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS
  alternative_names_per_language jsonb DEFAULT '{}';
-- {
--   "th": ["TMJ", "ขากรรไกรค้าง", "ข้อต่อขากรรไกรเสื่อม"],
--   "en": ["TMJ", "TMD", "Jaw joint disorder"]
-- }

ALTER TABLE seo_entity_graph ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS
  search_volume_per_language jsonb DEFAULT '{}';
-- DataForSEO tracking per language market:
-- {
--   "th": {"monthly_volume": 5400, "trend": "stable"},
--   "en": {"monthly_volume": 12000, "trend": "rising"}
-- }
```

### 28.3.3 Query Patterns

```sql
-- Render entity name for current page language
SELECT 
  COALESCE(
    canonical_names->>$1,           -- requested language
    canonical_names->>'en',          -- fallback to English
    canonical_names->>'th'           -- fallback to Thai
  ) as display_name
FROM seo_entity_graph
WHERE entity_fingerprint = $2;

-- Find entities missing translation
SELECT entity_fingerprint, canonical_names
FROM seo_entity_graph
WHERE NOT (canonical_names ? 'en')   -- missing English
  AND brand_scope @> ARRAY['vth-biodent']
LIMIT 100;
```

## 28.4 Translation Workflow (AI-Draft + Human Review)

### 28.4.1 Workflow Stages

```yaml
stage_1_thai_creation_(default):
  who: Thai-language editor
  where: Notion (Entities DB or Pages DB)
  what: Create entity/page in Thai with full content
  status: draft → ready_for_publish (Thai-only initially)
  
  fields_filled:
    - canonical_names.th = "โรค TMJ"
    - descriptions.th = full Thai description
    - All ACF content fields in Thai
  
  quality_gates:
    - Editorial review (Bible Part 23.4)
    - Citation verification
    - Medical accuracy check (if applicable)

stage_2_english_ai_draft:
  trigger: 
    - automatic on Thai approval (configurable)
    - OR manual flag: "needs_english_translation"
  
  process:
    - n8n flow calls AI translation API:
      Source: Anthropic Claude (recommended for medical context)
      Alternative: GPT-4, DeepL (medical-grade)
    - Input: Thai canonical_name + description + key fields
    - Output: English draft populated to:
      - canonical_names.en
      - descriptions.en
      - Other translatable ACF fields
  
  status: translation_status = 'machine_translated'
  flag: needs_human_review = true

stage_3_human_review:
  who: bilingual reviewer (medical professional preferred)
  where: Notion English view of same entity
  
  review_checklist:
    □ Medical terminology accurate
    □ Brand voice preserved
    □ Tone appropriate (formal/clinical)
    □ Cultural appropriateness
    □ Idioms/phrases natural
    □ Numbers/units converted (if needed)
    □ References (Thai-only references replaced or kept)
  
  actions:
    - Edit incorrect translations
    - Refine clunky phrasing
    - Verify medical terms against authoritative sources
  
  on_complete:
    translation_status = 'human_reviewed'
    needs_human_review = false

stage_4_publish_to_wordpress:
  via: n8n flow + WPML REST API integration
  
  creates:
    - Thai post (default URL)
    - English post (linked via WPML)
    - hreflang tags auto-generated
    - Schema includes inLanguage + sameAs
  
  result: both languages live simultaneously

stage_5_ongoing_maintenance:
  thai_content_update: 
    → flag English version as 'needs_review' if change is significant
  
  english_only_update:
    → done in English Notion view
    → no impact on Thai version
```

### 28.4.2 AI Translation Configuration

```yaml
ai_translation_provider:
  primary: Anthropic Claude (claude-sonnet-4-7)
  fallback: GPT-4
  
  prompt_template: |
    You are a medical translator specializing in Thai-English translation 
    for healthcare content. Translate the following from {source_lang} to 
    {target_lang}, preserving:
    
    1. Medical accuracy and clinical terminology
    2. Brand voice (professional, empathetic, expert)
    3. SEO keyword intent (do not translate proper nouns or branded terms)
    4. Cultural appropriateness for {target_market}
    5. Patient-friendly language (avoid jargon when possible)
    
    Keep these terms untranslated:
    - Brand names (e.g., VTH BioDent, Mouth Bio Mapping, EmSmile)
    - Medical device brands (e.g., Solea, BioPak)
    - ICD-10 codes
    - Drug brand names (use generic name in target language)
    
    Source text ({source_lang}):
    {source_text}
    
    Provide ONLY the translation, no commentary.
  
  cost_estimate:
    avg_tokens_per_entity: 500-2000 (description + fields)
    cost_per_1k_tokens: ~$0.003 (Claude Sonnet)
    300_entities × 2_languages: ~$5-15 per brand initial draft
    ongoing: ~$2-5/month per brand (incremental updates)

quality_checks:
  automatic:
    - Length sanity (translated text not <30% or >300% of source)
    - No untranslated chunks (catch AI failure)
    - Markdown formatting preserved
    - Links preserved
  
  manual_review_triggers:
    - Medical claim sentences (high-risk content)
    - Citation quotes (preserve verbatim)
    - Disclaimer text (legal precision needed)
    - Pillar pages (E-E-A-T sensitive)
```

## 28.5 WPML Configuration for EYWA CPTs

### 28.5.1 Per-CPT Translation Settings

```yaml
wpml_translation_management:
  
  always_translate_(content):
    - condition           # medical content, full translation
    - procedure           # treatment descriptions
    - treatment           # care pathways
    - case_study          # patient stories
    - post                # knowledge content
    - program             # branded programs (Tier 2)
    - signature_system    # branded methodologies
  
  translate_with_special_handling:
    - doctor:
        translate: bio, credentials descriptions
        copy_once: doctor photo, name (transliteration)
        sync: specialty taxonomy
    
    - branch:
        translate: branch description, parking notes
        copy_once: address, phone, GPS coordinates, photos
        adjust_per_language: operating_hours format
  
  translate_carefully_(vertical_specific):
    - ingredient          # technical names + descriptions
    - drug                # generic names + brand names
    - lab_test            # test names + procedures
    - product             # product descriptions
    - technology          # device descriptions

never_translate_(universal):
  - taxonomies (use term IDs across languages):
    sitemap_section, layer, tier, funnel_stage, lifecycle_state
  - URL slugs of doctors, branches (transliteration kept)
  - SKUs, codes, IDs
```

### 28.5.2 ACF + WPML Field Translation Rules

```yaml
acf_field_translation_settings:
  
  translate_per_language_(Translation_Editor):
    field_types:
      - text, textarea, wysiwyg
      - email, url
      - select, radio (label translation)
      - repeater (subfields translated individually)
    
    examples:
      - canonical_name → translated
      - description → translated
      - faq_repeater (question + answer per row) → translated
      - meta_description → translated
      - hero_subtitle → translated
  
  copy_(same_value_all_languages):
    field_types:
      - number
      - true_false
      - date_picker
      - color_picker
      - relationship (post connections)
      - taxonomy (term connections)
    
    examples:
      - publication_date → same across languages
      - icd_10_code → universal
      - entity_authority_score → computed once
      - reviewed_by (relationship) → same doctor
      - tier_evidence → universal classification
  
  copy_once_(initial_value_then_independent):
    field_types:
      - image, gallery (with separate alt_text per language)
      - file
    
    note: 
      - Image asset same across languages
      - alt_text translated per language (separate ACF field)
  
  not_translated_(language_specific_value):
    examples:
      - search_volume (different per market!)
      - keyword_difficulty (different per market)
      - local_keyword_target (different per market)
      - cultural_context_notes (per language)

configuration_in_wpml:
  WPML > Settings > Custom Fields Translation:
    For each ACF field: set Translation behavior
    
  Best practice:
    Configure ACF field group → Translation Preferences
    Once configured, all fields in group inherit settings
    Override individually if needed
```

## 28.6 hreflang Strategy

### 28.6.1 Auto-Generation by WPML

```yaml
hreflang_auto_generated:
  source: WPML (automatic)
  validation: RankMath Pro
  
  rendered_in_html_head:
    <link rel="alternate" hreflang="th" href="https://vth-biodent.com/knowledge/tmj/" />
    <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en" href="https://vth-biodent.com/en/knowledge/tmj/" />
    <link rel="alternate" hreflang="x-default" href="https://vth-biodent.com/knowledge/tmj/" />
  
  rules:
    - Every translated page declares all alternates
    - x-default points to Thai (default language)
    - hreflang codes use ISO 639-1 (2-letter)
    - For regional variants: th-TH, en-US, etc. (if needed)
```

### 28.6.2 Validation Workflow

```yaml
validation_layers:
  
  layer_1_automatic:
    - WPML generates on every page render
    - hreflang_validated field tracks per page
  
  layer_2_rankmath:
    - RankMath Pro validates hreflang setup
    - Flags missing translations
    - Flags broken hreflang chains
  
  layer_3_eywa_n8n:
    - Daily flow checks Google Search Console
    - Reports hreflang errors
    - Alerts editorial team
  
  layer_4_manual_audit:
    - Quarterly hreflang health check
    - Tools: Screaming Frog, Sitebulb
    - Cross-reference with sitemap
```

### 28.6.3 Common Issues & Mitigations

```yaml
issue_1_missing_translation:
  symptom: Thai page exists, English version missing
  hreflang_impact: only Thai version declares hreflang (incomplete)
  mitigation:
    - Editorial flag: "missing_english_translation"
    - n8n daily report
    - Block hreflang publication until both languages ready (config option)

issue_2_broken_hreflang_chain:
  symptom: Thai → English declared, English → Thai missing
  hreflang_impact: Google ignores (must be reciprocal)
  mitigation:
    - WPML normally handles correctly
    - RankMath validates chain
    - Manual audit if errors persist

issue_3_redirect_in_hreflang:
  symptom: hreflang URL redirects (301/302)
  hreflang_impact: Google de-prioritizes
  mitigation:
    - Always use canonical (final) URL in hreflang
    - n8n daily HTTP HEAD validation

issue_4_rtl_language_(arabic):
  symptom: Arabic content rendered LTR
  hreflang_impact: none directly
  layout_impact: significant
  mitigation:
    - Hello theme RTL ready
    - WPML handles dir="rtl" automatically
    - Test in Elementor preview before publish
```

## 28.7 Schema Markup Multilingual

### 28.7.1 Per-Page Schema Pattern

```javascript
// EYWA Schema Pipeline output for Thai page

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "MedicalCondition",
  "@id": "https://vth-biodent.com/by-concern/tmj-disorder/#condition",
  
  // Language declaration
  "inLanguage": "th",
  
  // Localized name + alternates
  "name": "โรคข้อต่อขากรรไกร",
  "alternateName": ["TMJ", "ขากรรไกรค้าง"],
  
  // Localized description
  "description": "...",
  
  // Universal identifiers (cross-language)
  "code": [
    {"@type": "MedicalCode", "codeValue": "DA0E.8", "codingSystem": "ICD-11-MMS"},
    {"@type": "MedicalCode", "codeValue": "K07.6", "codingSystem": "ICD-10"},
    {"@type": "MedicalCode", "codeValue": "M26.6", "codingSystem": "ICD-10-CM"}
  ],
  "sameAs": [
    "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q768229",   // Universal identifier
    "https://vth-biodent.com/en/by-concern/tmj-disorder/#condition"  // English version
  ],
  
  // Translation linkage
  "workTranslation": [
    {
      "@type": "MedicalCondition",
      "@id": "https://vth-biodent.com/en/by-concern/tmj-disorder/#condition",
      "inLanguage": "en",
      "name": "Temporomandibular Joint Disorder"
    }
  ]
}
```

### 28.7.2 Schema Pipeline Multilingual Logic

```yaml
eywa_schema_pipeline_multilingual:
  
  per_page_render:
    detect_language: get current page language from WPML
    
    pull_from_acf:
      - canonical_name (in current language)
      - description (in current language)
      - other localized fields
    
    pull_universal:
      - icd_10_code (same)
      - wikidata_id (same)
      - schema.org type (same)
      - publication_date (same)
    
    generate_alternates:
      - For each translated version:
        Get URL via WPML API
        Add to sameAs array
        Add to workTranslation array
    
    output:
      <script type="application/ld+json">
        { ... full schema with multilingual support }
      </script>

caching:
  per language + per page = separate cache entries
  invalidation: when ACF field updates in any language
```

## 28.8 Citation Language Handling

### 28.8.1 Multilingual Citation Strategy

```yaml
citation_language_decisions:
  
  english_citations_on_thai_page:
    status: ACCEPTABLE (recommended in many cases)
    rationale:
      - PubMed papers primarily English
      - Authoritative medical sources English-dominant
      - Thai readers expect English citations for credibility
      - Google understands cross-language citations
    
    presentation:
      - Show English citation as-is
      - Optional: Thai annotation: "(งานวิจัยภาษาอังกฤษ)"
      - Translate quote selectively (if used inline)
  
  thai_citations_on_thai_page:
    status: PREFERRED when available
    sources:
      - Thai medical journals
      - Thai Ministry of Health publications
      - Royal College of Physicians of Thailand
    
    presentation: native Thai text
  
  thai_citations_on_english_page:
    status: USE CAUTIOUSLY
    rationale: 
      - English readers may not access Thai sources
      - Reduce credibility for international audience
    
    handling:
      - Provide English title translation
      - Note "(in Thai)" disclosure
      - Prefer English alternative if available
  
  citation_database_storage:
    seo_citations.language: 'en' / 'th' / 'zh' / etc.
    seo_citations.title: native title (in original language)
    seo_citations.title_translations: jsonb (translated titles)
```

### 28.8.2 EYWA Citation Authority Weight (Multilingual)

```yaml
extended_formula_for_multilingual:
  
  base_citation_authority_weight (Bible Part 27.6.1):
    [tier weight × freshness modifier]
  
  multilingual_adjustment:
    same_language_as_page: × 1.0  (no penalty)
    different_language_translated: × 0.95
    different_language_untranslated: × 0.85
    universal_authority (PubMed, WHO): × 1.0  (regardless of language)
  
  rationale:
    - Universal authority sources don't suffer language penalty
    - Translated sources ~95% as effective
    - Untranslated cross-language ~85% (less accessible to readers)

implementation:
  citation_authority_weight = 
    base_weight × language_modifier
```

## 28.9 Multilingual EYWA Scoring

### 28.9.1 Per-Language Scoring Strategy

```yaml
scoring_decision: COMPUTE PER LANGUAGE + AGGREGATE

rationale:
  - Thai performance ≠ English performance
  - Different markets, different signals
  - Resource allocation needs per-language visibility
  - Aggregate provides portfolio view

storage_pattern:
  
  entity_authority_score_th: numeric
  entity_authority_score_en: numeric
  entity_authority_score: numeric
    -- aggregate strategy: max(per_language_scores)
    -- alternative: weighted by traffic share
  
  Same pattern for:
    e_e_a_t_score_*
    content_quality_score_*
    cluster_health_score_*
    brand_authority_score_*
    ai_citation_readiness_*
```

### 28.9.2 Per-Language Compute Logic

```sql
-- Example: entity_authority_score_th computation
-- Same formula as Bible Part 27.2.1 BUT scoped to Thai data

CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION compute_entity_authority_per_language_v1(
  p_entity_fp text,
  p_brand_id text,
  p_language text
) RETURNS jsonb AS $$
DECLARE
  v_factors jsonb;
  v_score numeric;
BEGIN
  -- Factor 1: Internal Coverage (pages in this language)
  -- Factor 2: Edge in-degree (universal — same across languages)
  -- Factor 3: Citation density (citations on this language's pages)
  -- Factor 4: Search volume (DataForSEO data for this language market)
  -- Factor 5: External authority (backlinks to this language's pages)
  -- Factor 6: AI citation rate (in this language by AI engines)
  
  -- ... (full computation per language scope)
  
  RETURN jsonb_build_object(
    'score', v_score,
    'language', p_language,
    'factors', v_factors,
    'formula_version', 'v1.0-multilingual'
  );
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Aggregate score: max across languages
UPDATE seo_entity_graph SET
  entity_authority_score = GREATEST(
    COALESCE(entity_authority_score_th, 0),
    COALESCE(entity_authority_score_en, 0)
  )
WHERE entity_fingerprint = $1;
```

### 28.9.3 Cross-Language Insights

```yaml
operator_dashboards_(multilingual):
  
  per_brand_per_language_breakdown:
    "VTH Thai: brand_authority = 78"
    "VTH English: brand_authority = 45"
    → English market underperforming, allocate resources
  
  cluster_strength_comparison:
    "TMJ cluster — Thai: 85, English: 32"
    → English TMJ content needs investment
  
  citation_balance:
    "Thai pages: 60% citations from Thai sources"
    "English pages: 80% citations from international sources"
    → balanced, appropriate
  
  ai_citation_visibility:
    "Thai AI queries: VTH cited 35% of time"
    "English AI queries: VTH cited 12% of time"
    → significant English-side opportunity
```

## 28.10 Elementor + WPML Template Strategy

### 28.10.1 Single Template, Dynamic Content

```yaml
template_strategy_locked:
  pattern: ONE Elementor template per CPT (not per language)
  
  how_it_works:
    1. Designer creates single-doctor template once
    2. WPML translates ACF field values per language
    3. Dynamic Tags pull translated values automatically
    4. Same layout renders in all languages
  
  benefits:
    ✅ Maintain ONE template = faster updates
    ✅ Layout consistency across languages
    ✅ No drift between language versions
    ✅ Simpler version control

what_changes_per_language:
  - Text content (via Dynamic Tags pulling translated ACF)
  - Image alt text (via translated ACF alt field)
  - Date format (via WPML locale settings)
  - Number format (via WPML locale)
  - RTL flip for Arabic (automatic via WPML + Hello theme)

what_stays_same_per_language:
  - Layout structure
  - Widget arrangement
  - Color palette (Site Settings)
  - Typography (Site Settings, with locale-specific font fallbacks)
```

### 28.10.2 Language Switcher Implementation

```yaml
elementor_language_switcher:
  widget: WPML Language Switcher (Elementor-compatible)
  position: header (consistent placement across templates)
  
  display_options:
    style: flag + native language name
    show_only_translated: true (don't show language without translation)
    current_language_display: highlighted
  
  example:
    [TH 🇹🇭] [EN 🇺🇸] [ZH 🇨🇳]
    Active language has different styling
```

### 28.10.3 RTL Considerations (Arabic)

```yaml
rtl_support_for_arabic:
  
  what_handles_automatically:
    - WPML detects Arabic = RTL language
    - Adds dir="rtl" to <html>
    - Hello Elementor theme switches layout
    - Elementor Pro RTL mode: layout mirrors
    - Icons/buttons swap sides automatically
  
  manual_considerations:
    - Brand logo: typically don't mirror
    - Phone numbers: keep LTR within RTL context
    - English text within Arabic: needs <span dir="ltr">
    - Number formatting: Arabic-Indic numerals or Western
  
  testing_checklist_when_arabic_added:
    □ Layout flips correctly
    □ Navigation menu mirrors
    □ Form fields align right
    □ Icons swap sides (chevrons, arrows)
    □ Mixed-direction content (English in Arabic) renders cleanly
    □ Schema markup includes dir="rtl"

elementor_rtl_setup:
  WordPress > Settings > General > Site Language: 'العربية'
  WPML > Languages > Arabic: enabled, RTL set
  Hello theme: detects automatically
  Elementor: switches editor to RTL mode automatically
  Custom CSS: use logical properties (margin-inline-start vs margin-left)
```

## 28.11 DataForSEO Multilingual Tracking

### 28.11.1 Per-Language DataForSEO Setup

```yaml
dataforseo_multilingual_strategy:
  
  separate_tracking_streams:
    
    backlinks:
      query_targets: 
        - vth-biodent.com/* (universal)
        - vth-biodent.com/en/* (English-specific)
        - vth-biodent.com/zh/* (Chinese-specific)
      
      analysis: backlinks per language section
      benefit: identify language-specific link gaps
    
    rankings:
      separate_location_language_combinations:
        - location: Thailand, language: Thai
        - location: Thailand, language: English (medical tourism)
        - location: Singapore, language: English (regional)
        - location: China, language: Chinese (medical tourism)
      
      tracked_keywords:
        Thai keywords: "การรักษา TMJ", "หมอฟันเชี่ยวชาญ TMJ"
        English keywords: "TMJ treatment Bangkok", "best TMJ specialist Thailand"
        Chinese keywords: tracked when zh launches
    
    keyword_volume:
      query_per_target_market:
        - search_volume in Thai (TH market)
        - search_volume in English (US/UK/SG markets)
      
      stored_in: search_volume_per_language jsonb
    
    domain_rank:
      tracked_at_domain_level (universal)
      interpreted_per_language: 
        - Thai-language strength
        - English-language strength
        - Cross-reference per language section
```

### 28.11.2 n8n Flow Pattern (Multilingual)

```yaml
flow_dataforseo_multilingual_sync:
  schedule: daily for rankings, weekly for backlinks
  
  per_brand_loop:
    for each brand:
      get active_languages from brand_profile
      
      for each language in active_languages:
        # Rankings
        fetch_serp_rankings(
          domain=brand.domain,
          location=language_to_market[language],
          language_code=language,
          path_filter=f"/{language}/*"  # if not default lang
        )
        store in seo_x_ads_keywords_x_url_daily_logs (with language tag)
        
        # Keyword research (less frequent)
        if keyword_refresh_due:
          fetch_keyword_volume(
            keywords=brand.tracked_keywords[language],
            location=language_to_market[language],
            language=language
          )
          update search_volume_per_language jsonb on entities
      
      # Backlinks (universal + per-language)
      fetch_backlinks(target=brand.domain)
      categorize by language section
      store with language attribution
```

# PART 29: Ads Landing Page Track 🆕 v3.16

> **Per DR-026 (Proposed 2026-05-12)** — parallel implementation track to SEO. Same dimensional backbone (`seo_page_master` + `seo_x_ads_keywords_contextual_master` + `seo_entity_graph`); additive columns; dedicated template family `T-ADS-X`.
>
> **Companion DRs:** DR-026 (this Part), DR-027 (Future Phase 1: `seo_campaigns` Universal Master)
> **Companion Schema:** v1.12 (additive columns; no new tables in Phase 0)
> **Companion Templates:** v1.4 (T-ADS-1 through T-ADS-5)

## 29.1 Why Ads-LP Is a Parallel Track (not a substitute for SEO)

EYWA's SEO track (Parts 1-28) optimizes for organic discoverability, topical authority, E-E-A-T signals, and AI citation. The Ads track optimizes for **paid acquisition conversion** — a different objective with different page-level constraints.

| Dimension | SEO Track (T1-T22) | Ads Track (T-ADS-1 to T-ADS-5) |
|-----------|--------------------|---------------------------------|
| **Goal** | Rank + authority + topical depth + AI citation | Maximize CVR from paid click |
| **Audience** | Cold/warm — researching | Hot — clicked Ad with specific promise |
| **Structure** | Hub-spoke, internal links, schema depth | Single CTA, scannable, focused offer |
| **Content depth** | 1,500-4,000+ words (per Part 19/Bible §6) | 200-900 words (per template) |
| **CTA pattern** | Multiple soft CTAs (subscribe, read more, related) | ONE primary CTA, repeated 2-3x |
| **Navigation** | Full site nav | Stripped or minimal nav |
| **Index policy** | indexed permanent | `noindex_lp` default (configurable) |
| **Quality Score** | not applicable | critical (Google Ads CPC driver) |
| **Schema markup** | MedicalProcedure / FAQPage / Article / etc. | Organization + Offer + LocalBusiness |
| **Lifecycle** | long-lived, refresh-via-DR-022 cycle | campaign-bound, often shorter-lived |

**Some pages can do both** — see §29.6 Dual-Use Eligibility Criteria.

## 29.2 Page Purpose Taxonomy

DR-026 introduces the `page_purpose` enum on `seo_page_master`:

```yaml
page_purpose:
  seo_organic:
    description: Pure SEO page — indexed, hub-spoke, topical authority
    template_family: T1-T22
    index_directive: index
    nav_treatment: full site nav
    cta_count: multiple soft

  ads_lp:
    description: Pure Ads landing page — conversion-optimized
    template_family: T-ADS-1 to T-ADS-5
    index_directive: noindex_lp (default; operator can override)
    nav_treatment: stripped or minimal
    cta_count: ONE primary, repeated 2-3x

  dual_use:
    description: Page serves both SEO + Ads
    template_family: hybrid (see §29.6)
    index_directive: index
    nav_treatment: full site nav
    cta_count: dominant primary + supporting SEO depth
    eligibility_gate: §29.6 (6 criteria)
```

## 29.3 URL Convention

```yaml
seo_organic: /{vertical-slug}/{topic-slug}/   # Part 4 convention unchanged
ads_lp:      /lp/{campaign-or-offer-slug}/    # NEW — `/lp/` marks Ads track
dual_use:    existing SEO URL (no change — flagged via page_purpose)
```

**Why `/lp/` prefix:**

- Visual signal to operators + legal + analytics teams
- Easy regex for Quality Score audits + robots.txt directives
- Report segmentation (organic traffic vs paid traffic by URL pattern)
- Optional bulk `noindex` via single rule when needed

**Naming convention for `{campaign-or-offer-slug}`:** kebab-case, brand-scoped enough to be self-explanatory, with optional date suffix for time-bound offers.

```
/lp/dental-implant-free-consult/             ✅ generic offer LP
/lp/blue-diamond-29900-may-2026/             ✅ time-bound promo
/lp/men-vitality-package-bangkok/             ✅ geo-targeted LP
/lp/lp-1/                                    ❌ non-descriptive
/lp/test-page-final-v2/                       ❌ temporary scratchpad name
```

## 29.4 Index Directive

`index_directive` enum on `seo_page_master`:

| Value | `<meta robots>` | Sitemap.xml | Use case |
|-------|----------------|------------|----------|
| `index` | `index, follow` | included | Default for `seo_organic` + `dual_use` |
| `noindex_lp` | `noindex, follow` | EXCLUDED | Default for `ads_lp` — link equity flows |
| `noindex_nofollow` | `noindex, nofollow` | EXCLUDED | A/B variants, ephemeral test pages |
| `dual` | `index, follow` | included | Rare — `dual_use` confirmed dual-serving |

**Default policy:** `ads_lp` pages with `index_directive=noindex_lp` are EXCLUDED from XML sitemap. Operator can override for evergreen LPs that should compete in organic SERP as well.

## 29.5 Conversion Event Taxonomy

`conversion_event_primary` enum + `conversion_event_secondary text[]`:

```yaml
lead_form:    form submission (incl. Typeform, native, etc.)
call_click:   phone CTA tap
line_follow:  LINE Add Friend / chat-initiate
booking:      appointment booking submitted
download:     lead magnet download (T-ADS-5)
package_view: pricing/package PDF view (high-intent intermediate)
add_to_cart:  e-commerce (rare in EYWA portfolio)
```

Maps to:
- **Google Ads Conversion Actions** (Primary + Secondary classification)
- **Meta Pixel Standard Events** (Lead, Contact, Subscribe, CompleteRegistration, Purchase)
- **GA4 events** (`generate_lead`, `contact`, `add_to_cart`, custom names per brand)

Every `ads_lp` page MUST declare `conversion_event_primary` at page-master row creation. `conversion_event_secondary` is optional (max 3 — discourage over-tracking).

## 29.6 Dual-Use Eligibility Criteria

A page can be marked `page_purpose='dual_use'` ONLY when ALL 6 criteria are satisfied:

| # | Criterion | Measurement |
|---|-----------|-------------|
| 1 | **Intent match** | Page targets commercial/transactional KW (not informational) — see `ad_intent_score ≥ 7` per §29.7 |
| 2 | **CTA prominence** | Primary CTA visible above mobile fold + repeated at 1-2 mid-page positions |
| 3 | **Conversion infra** | Conversion tracking pixel/event installed; all CTAs wired (form/phone/LINE) to GTM |
| 4 | **CWV pass** | LCP < 2.5s mobile, CLS < 0.1, INP < 200ms (Part 19 standards) |
| 5 | **Content focus** | Single dominant offer — NOT a hub page listing 10 services |
| 6 | **Quality Score viability** | Google Ads QS ≥ 7 after 2-week stabilization; if < 7 for 4+ weeks → demote to `seo_organic`, build parallel `/lp/` version |

Operator MUST document the dual-use justification in `viability_assessment` column (Part 4.14 column reused) at the time of marking. Demotion (criterion 6 fails) is operator workflow, not auto.

## 29.7 Keyword Schema Extensions (per DR-026)

Additive columns on `seo_x_ads_keywords_contextual_master`:

```yaml
seo_active boolean default true
  description: Keyword is in SEO content strategy

ad_active boolean default false
  description: Keyword is in active Ads bidding

ad_intent_score smallint
  range: 1-10
  semantic:
    10 = transactional/commercial — buyer-ready
    7  = strong commercial intent (research-with-purchase-mode)
    5  = mixed informational/commercial
    3  = informational research
    1  = pure educational, no commercial intent
  default: NULL (operator scores during KW research; required before ad_active=true)

ad_match_type_preferred enum (exact | phrase | broad | broad_modified)
  description: Planning-time preference; actual platform match enforced at campaign level

ad_landing_page_fp text nullable
  description: FK → seo_page_master.fingerprint — the LP intended for this KW (Phase 0; Phase 1 moves to seo_campaign_keywords M2M)

ad_priority_tier enum (t1 | t2 | t3 | none)
  semantic:
    t1 = always-on hero KW (top budget priority)
    t2 = supporting (sustained budget)
    t3 = exploratory / testing
    none = SEO-only (no ad)
```

**Dual-flag pattern:** A keyword can have `seo_active=true` AND `ad_active=true` simultaneously — that is the canonical "shared use" case. `seo_active` should default true (most KWs in EYWA are SEO-led). `ad_active` defaults false (Ads is opt-in per KW).

## 29.8 Page Schema Extensions (per DR-026)

Additive columns on `seo_page_master`:

```yaml
page_purpose enum (seo_organic | ads_lp | dual_use)
  default: seo_organic

ads_template_id text nullable
  values: T-ADS-1 | T-ADS-2 | T-ADS-3 | T-ADS-4 | T-ADS-5 | T-DUAL-{N} (future hybrid)
  required_when: page_purpose IN (ads_lp, dual_use)

index_directive enum (index | noindex_lp | noindex_nofollow | dual)
  default: index

conversion_event_primary enum (lead_form | call_click | line_follow | booking | download | package_view | add_to_cart)
  required_when: page_purpose IN (ads_lp, dual_use)

conversion_event_secondary text[] nullable
  constraint: max 3 entries

campaign_id text nullable
  description: TRANSITIONAL STUB — Phase 0 placeholder for campaign association
  format: "{brand-id}-{purpose}-{date-suffix}" recommended (e.g., "vth-biodent-launch-2026-q2")
  future_state: per DR-027, this column becomes campaign_fp text FK → seo_campaigns when DR-027 ships
  migration_safety: parse distinct values, create seo_campaigns rows, populate junction
```

## 29.9 T-ADS Template Family (overview — full specs in Content_Templates v1.4)

5 templates ship Phase 0:

| Template | Purpose | Word target | Schema |
|----------|---------|-------------|--------|
| **T-ADS-1** Hero Service LP | Single-service conversion | 400-800 | Org + LocalBusiness + Offer + MedicalBusiness (medical) |
| **T-ADS-2** Booking / Consultation LP | Drive appointment booking | 300-600 | Org + Offer + Person (doctor) |
| **T-ADS-3** Promo / Limited Offer LP | Time-bound offer (countdown, scarcity) | 350-700 | Org + Offer (`priceValidUntil`) |
| **T-ADS-4** Comparison / Alternative LP | Win clicks from competitor / alt-seeking | 500-900 | Org (no Offer if pure positioning) |
| **T-ADS-5** Lead Magnet / Download LP | Email/LINE capture for downloadable | 200-400 | Org + CreativeWork/ImageObject |

**Block-structure details, render examples, and ACF mappings:** see `Content_Templates_EYWA_v1_0.md` §T-ADS-X.

## 29.10 YMYL Evidence Rules — UNCHANGED for Ads LPs

> **CRITICAL:** Bible Part 23 (Medical Content Excellence) citation tier rules + editorial review workflow apply IDENTICALLY to Ads LPs that make medical claims.

Ads LPs do NOT get a YMYL exemption. Rationale:

- **PDPA + medical advertising law** (พรบ. การโฆษณาทางการแพทย์) applies regardless of URL pattern
- **Google Ads medical claim policies** enforce accuracy on landing pages, not just ad copy
- **Brand legal exposure** is per-claim, not per-URL — moving a claim to `/lp/` does not reduce risk

**Operational implication:**

- Tier 1-3 citation requirement (Bible Part 23.1) applies to every medical claim on T-ADS-1/2/3/4
- Editorial review (Bible Part 23.4) required before Ads LP goes live
- Comparative claims on T-ADS-4 must comply with Bible Part 23.5 (no disparagement, use public factual info only)
- PDPA consent banner (Bible Part 23.6) MANDATORY on T-ADS-5 (lead capture) and T-ADS-2 (booking form)

## 29.11 Future: Campaign Master Track (Phase 1 — DR-027 placeholder)

Phase 0 (this Part) is sufficient for a brand to launch Google Ads with structured LP + KW tracking. Phase 0 is NOT sufficient for:

1. **Multi-platform campaign orchestration** — Google Ads + Meta Ads + YouTube + LINE + TikTok with shared budget envelope
2. **Cross-platform consolidated reporting** — performance snapshot per platform aggregated to campaign level
3. **Junction between campaigns ↔ pages ↔ keywords** — 1 campaign : N LPs : M keywords
4. **Historical performance archival** — Supabase-hosted daily snapshot rows

**DR-027 reserves architecture for Phase 1:**

```yaml
seo_campaigns:
  identity: campaign_fp text PK
  brand: brand_id FK → brands.id
  classification: platforms text[], objective enum, audience_tier enum
  financial: budget_total_thb, budget_per_platform jsonb, budget_pacing enum
  schedule: date_start, date_end, status enum
  governance: approved_by_fp, approval_date

seo_campaign_pages (M2M):    campaign_fp × page_fp + role enum
seo_campaign_keywords (M2M): campaign_fp × keyword_fp + platform + match_type + bid_strategy
seo_campaign_performance_snapshot: daily per campaign per platform (mirrors keyword_daily_logs)
```

**Migration path from Phase 0 → Phase 1:**

When DR-027 ships:

1. Parse distinct values of `seo_page_master.campaign_id` (TEXT stub) across all brand rows
2. Create `seo_campaigns` rows for each distinct campaign label
3. Populate `seo_campaign_pages` junction from existing `page_master` rows where `campaign_id IS NOT NULL`
4. Populate `seo_campaign_keywords` from any KW rows already flagged `ad_active=true` with `ad_landing_page_fp` set
5. Replace `seo_page_master.campaign_id text` with `campaign_fp text FK → seo_campaigns` (alter column type with mapping)

**Naming convention for Phase 0 `campaign_id` (CRITICAL for clean migration):**

```
{brand-id}-{purpose}-{date-suffix}

Examples:
  vth-biodent-launch-2026-q2
  smilescape-blue-diamond-promo-2026-may
  trin-wellness-vital-core-evergreen
```

Brands MUST adopt this naming convention from day 1. Free-form labels make Phase 1 migration painful.

## 29.12 Brand Implementation Workflow (Phase 0)

When a brand decides to launch Google Ads:

```yaml
step_1_planning:
  scope: identify hero offer + 2-5 LPs needed
  outputs:
    - LP page rows in Notion (page_purpose=ads_lp, ads_template_id=T-ADS-X, campaign_id set)
    - Keyword rows flagged (ad_active=true, ad_intent_score, ad_priority_tier, ad_landing_page_fp)
  dependencies:
    - Brand Stage 1 Phase A complete (brand-concept.md)
    - KW research done (at least Layer 1 brand-immune KWs known)
    - At least 1 doctor profile published (Person schema source for T-ADS-2)

step_2_content_production:
  scope: write LP content per T-ADS template
  YMYL_gate: Part 23 review for medical claims
  PDPA_gate: consent banner mandatory if LP has form/booking
  outputs:
    - Content brief per LP (T-ADS section of Content_Templates v1.4)
    - Reviewed + approved content (editorial workflow)

step_3_deployment:
  scope: build LP in CMS, install conversion tracking, configure index_directive
  CWV_gate: must pass Part 19 standards (LCP/CLS/INP)
  outputs:
    - Live LP at /lp/{slug}/
    - Conversion events firing (Google Ads Conv API + Meta Pixel + GA4)
    - Quality Score baseline established after 1 week

step_4_optimization:
  scope: monitor QS, CVR, CPA per LP
  duration: minimum 2-week stabilization before optimization edits
  outputs:
    - per-LP performance baseline (manual until DR-027 ships)
    - dual_use promotion candidate flag (if seo_organic page eligible per §29.6)
```

# PART 30: Brand Genesis Protocol (BGP) 🆕 v3.20

> **Per DR-028 (Locked 2026-05-17)** — Universal Brand onboarding methodology, parallel to EGP (Entity Genesis Protocol, Part 2.6). Replaces unstructured `brand-concept.md` with 5-deliverable structured Phase A. Ensures every brand engagement starts with brand+business+SEO triple-fit foundation.
>
> **Scope:** UNIVERSAL — applies to all brand repos AND eywa-marketing (EYWA dogfoods its own protocol)
> **Companion Bootstrap Kit:** `templates/folder-skeleton/docs/brand-genesis/` (5 template files)
> **Companion DR:** DR-028 (this Part's formalization)

## 30.1 Why BGP Exists (Parallel to EGP)

EGP (Part 2.6) operates on the **entity-knowledge layer** — produces structured entities, edges, taxonomies. BGP operates on the **brand-business layer** — produces structured brand DNA, business goals, alignment proof.

```
EGP (Entity Genesis Protocol)        BGP (Brand Genesis Protocol)
├── Operates on: entities + edges    ├── Operates on: brand DNA + business goals
├── Output: seo_entity_graph rows    ├── Output: 5 markdown deliverables
├── Question: "What concepts exist?" ├── Question: "What brand promise + business goal?"
└── Phase: B (post brand-concept)    └── Phase: A (the FOUNDATION for everything else)
```

**EGP feeds Knowledge Graph layer; BGP feeds Strategy + Editorial + Reporting layers.**

Without BGP, SEO drifts away from brand (voice violations, off-brand content) and from business (no ROI proof). With BGP, every SEO move traces back to alignment-map.md → business goal → brand promise → success metric.

## 30.2 The 5 Sub-Phases (Phase A.0 → A.4)

```
Phase A.0  ─→  Pre-Engagement Discovery     (1-2 hours)  →  business-context.md
   ↓
Phase A.1  ─→  EYWA DNA Graph workshop      (4-6 hours)  →  eywa-dna-graph.md
   ↓
Phase A.2  ─→  EYWA Framework Synapse       (2-3 hours)  →  framework-synapse.md
   ↓
Phase A.3  ─→  EYWA TRUST Rubric Baseline   (3-5 hours)  →  eywa-trust-rubric.md
   ↓
Phase A.4  ─→  Brand-Business-SEO Alignment (2-3 hours)  →  alignment-map.md
   ↓
Phase B-E  ─→  Existing EYWA flow (KW research → Entity Genesis → Sitemap → Content Plan)
                  ↑ now enriched by Phase A foundation; every page justified by alignment-map
```

**Total Phase A enhanced:** ~3 weeks (vs prior ~1 week). Phase B-E becomes faster because foundation is clearer.

## 30.3 Phase A.0 — Pre-Engagement Discovery

**Goal:** Capture context BEFORE bootstrap. Avoids assumptions later in Phase B-E.

**Deliverable:** `docs/brand-genesis/business-context.md`

**Outputs (template-driven):**

```yaml
business_goals:
  revenue_target_12mo: { value, currency, baseline }
  market_position_target: { competitor benchmark, desired rank }
  growth_horizon: { year-1, year-3, year-5 trajectory }

stakeholder_map:
  decision_makers: [name, role, decision_scope]
  gatekeepers: [name, role, gate_type]  # CFO controlling budget, MD controlling clinical claims
  end_users: [persona, primary_need]

constraints:
  budget: { monthly_marketing, one_time_setup, content_production_hours }
  timeline: { phase_b_deadline, first_content_live_target, full_launch_target }
  compliance: [PDPA, medical_advertising_law, brand-specific regulatory]
  technical: { existing_stack, migration_constraints, integration_points }

success_metrics:
  primary: "What does 'win' look like in 12 months?" (specific + measurable)
  secondary: [3-5 supporting metrics]
  reporting_cadence: { monthly | quarterly }
```

## 30.4 Phase A.1 — EYWA DNA Graph (Brand Key adapted)

**Goal:** Structured brand DNA in 10 fields. Single source of truth for all brand decisions downstream.

**Deliverable:** `docs/brand-genesis/eywa-dna-graph.md`

**10 Fields:**

| # | Field | Description | Example (Trin Wellness) |
|---|-------|-------------|------------------------|
| 1 | **Target Patient** | Demographic + psychographic | Thai men 30-60, mid-to-upper income, BKK metro, digitally savvy, health-conscious post-ED scare |
| 2 | **Patient Insight** | Deep truth / pain / unmet need | "ED is a symptom of something bigger but my GP just prescribed Viagra and sent me away" |
| 3 | **Clinical Benefits** | Functional outcomes — measurable | Root-cause diagnostic (vascular + hormone + metabolic) → treatment plan addressing systemic issue, not just symptom |
| 4 | **Emotional Benefits** | How patient feels after engagement | "Finally understood my body. Took charge instead of being prescribed away" |
| 5 | **Reasons to Trust (RTBs)** | Credentials, evidence, track record, social proof | Dr. Trin: vascular specialty + 20yr experience; 7 branded centers; ABI standalone tech; published outcomes |
| 6 | **Brand Personality** | 5-7 traits + 3-5 anti-traits | Trin = Diagnostic + Authoritative + Patient + Direct + Caring. Anti = Salesy, Quick-fix, Device-flashy |
| 7 | **Discriminator** | Single point of differentiation vs key competitors | "We don't sell shockwave. We find why ED happened, then treat the cause" |
| 8 | **Brand Essence** | One-line distilled identity | "The clinic that treats men by understanding men" |
| 9 | **Competitive Frame** | Which playing field we choose | Vs commodity ED clinics (HE/Menhance) → root-cause depth. Vs hospital wellness (BDMS/Vitallife) → male-specialty focus |
| 10 | **Compliance Boundaries** | What we CAN'T claim — healthcare YMYL discipline | No "cure" language for chronic conditions. No guaranteed outcomes. Must cite Tier 1-3 source for ED-CVD causality claims. No before/after without consent + anonymization |

**Field 10 is healthcare-specific** — adapted from Unilever Brand Key for YMYL discipline. Acts as published-content guardrail.

## 30.5 Phase A.2 — EYWA Framework Synapse

**Goal:** Document framework inputs that compose into EYWA's specific methodology. Makes implicit reasoning explicit.

**Deliverable:** `docs/brand-genesis/framework-synapse.md`

**Contains 3 inputs:**

### A.2.1 Golden Circle (Sinek, no rename)

```yaml
WHY: {brand purpose — single sentence why brand exists beyond making money}
HOW: {methodology — what's the unique way brand delivers}
WHAT: {services — concrete offerings}
```

### A.2.2 EYWA Intent Roots (Jobs-to-be-Done adapted)

```yaml
jobs_patient_hires_clinic_to_do:
  functional:
    - "fix this ED symptom"
    - "find a doctor who actually listens"
  emotional:
    - "feel in control of my body again"
    - "stop being embarrassed about a topic"
  social:
    - "be a better husband / partner"
    - "not be 'the guy who needs Viagra'"
```

### A.2.3 EYWA Journey Map (McKinsey CDJ adapted)

```yaml
stages:
  initial_consideration:
    triggers: [first ED episode, doctor mentions cardiovascular link, friend recommendation]
    touchpoints: [Google search, Pantip thread, friend talk, doctor referral]
    content_needs: [educational pillar — "Why ED happens", awareness — "Vascular link to ED"]

  active_evaluation:
    triggers: [comparing 2-3 clinics, reading reviews, checking credentials]
    touchpoints: [clinic websites, Google Maps reviews, Facebook posts, doctor profiles]
    content_needs: [credentials page, doctor profile depth, treatment comparison, pricing transparency]

  moment_of_purchase:
    triggers: [contact form filled, LINE Add Friend, phone call]
    touchpoints: [booking form, branch info, response speed, first-visit prep]
    content_needs: [booking CTA, branch info, FAQ on first visit, what to bring]

  post_purchase:
    triggers: [first visit done, treatment started, follow-up scheduled]
    touchpoints: [follow-up calls, LINE messages, treatment tracking]
    content_needs: [aftercare guides, progress tracking, what to expect]

  loyalty_loop:
    triggers: [outcomes achieved, referring friends, maintenance care]
    touchpoints: [periodic check-ins, alumni community, referral program]
    content_needs: [maintenance content, success stories, referral mechanism]
```

**Why this matters in Phase E (Content Plan):** Every page tagged with `cdj_stage` field. Sitemap audit ensures all stages have content coverage. Content Templates (Part 9) align with CDJ stage (e.g., T1 pillar → initial consideration; T2 service → active evaluation).

## 30.6 Phase A.3 — EYWA TRUST Rubric Baseline

**Goal:** Audit brand's current state across 5 pillars to identify SEO content gaps. First commercial deliverable of EYWA™ Audit tier.

**Deliverable:** `docs/brand-genesis/eywa-trust-rubric.md`

**5 Pillars:**

```yaml
T_trust:
  meaning: Medical authority + credentials + evidence-backed claims + citations
  scoring_signals:
    - Doctor credentials displayed with verifiable links
    - Tier 1-3 citations on medical claims (Bible Part 23.1)
    - Reviewed-by signoff on YMYL pages
    - Wikidata/sameAs/organization schema completeness
    - Years of experience + specialty depth visible
  score_band:
    0-3: Generic clinic, no credential depth
    4-6: Doctor names + basic credentials, some citations
    7-9: Specialist profiles + Tier 1-3 evidence per claim + sameAs schema
    10: Award-grade — recognized authority status (industry awards, published research)

R_results:
  meaning: Clinical outcomes + case studies + measurable success rates
  scoring_signals:
    - Documented patient outcomes (with PDPA-compliant anonymization)
    - Success rate statistics + sample size
    - Before/after evidence (visual or measurable)
    - Long-term outcome tracking
    - Peer-reviewed methodology where applicable
  score_band:
    0-3: No outcome documentation
    4-6: Generic testimonials, no measurable data
    7-9: Quantified outcomes + case studies + visual evidence (consented)
    10: Published outcomes data + audited methodology

U_understanding:
  meaning: Deep patient understanding + journey clarity + accessibility
  scoring_signals:
    - Patient persona depth visible in content tone
    - Journey-stage content coverage (per CDJ map)
    - Concern-led content (Section 5 Concerns per Part 4)
    - Accessibility (WCAG 2.1 AA — Bible Part 9)
    - Language clarity (no jargon barriers, multilingual where relevant)
  score_band:
    0-3: Generic content, single-persona
    4-6: Some persona segmentation, partial accessibility
    7-9: Full CDJ coverage + WCAG AA + bilingual + concern-led depth
    10: Adaptive personalization + multiple personas + accessibility audited

S_safety:
  meaning: Compliance + contraindications + disclosures + YMYL discipline
  scoring_signals:
    - Contraindications declared per procedure (per DR-013 edge type)
    - Safety disclosures on T2 service pages (per Content_Templates B25)
    - PDPA consent + privacy policy visible
    - Medical reviewer signoff on absolute contraindications (Bible §2.7.5)
    - Crisis disclosure on acute YMYL content (T1 with severe risk)
  score_band:
    0-3: Missing safety disclosures, regulatory risk
    4-6: Basic disclaimers, partial contraindication coverage
    7-9: Full contraindication edges + crisis disclosures + medical signoff workflow
    10: Comprehensive safety framework + regulatory audit pass

T_transparency:
  meaning: Pricing transparency + process clarity + data handling + PDPA
  scoring_signals:
    - Pricing visible (range OK — "start from X" acceptable per Bible Part 25)
    - Treatment process documented step-by-step
    - Data handling policy clear + PDPA compliance visible
    - Outcomes reporting transparent
    - Conflict of interest disclosures (e.g., sponsored research)
  score_band:
    0-3: No pricing, opaque process, no PDPA
    4-6: Partial pricing, basic process, PDPA banner
    7-9: Pricing tiers + full process + PDPA + data handling spec
    10: Full transparency + outcomes published + COI disclosed
```

**Per-pillar deliverable structure:**

```yaml
pillar_audit:
  pillar: T_trust
  current_score: 5
  evidence_of_score:
    - "Dr. Trin profile exists with ABRAM + A4M certifications visible"
    - "5 articles have Tier 2 citations (Journal of Sexual Medicine)"
  gaps_identified:
    - "No reviewedBy schema emission per YMYL page"
    - "Wikidata Q-number not claimed for Dr. Trin"
    - "Only 5/30 articles have Tier 1-3 citations"
  seo_content_opportunity:
    - "T9 Doctor profile expansion — add sameAs Wikidata + sameAs LinkedIn + peer review track"
    - "Citation backfill program — 25 articles need Tier 1-3 citation upgrade"
    - "ReviewedBy schema rollout — eywa-schema-pipeline plugin update"
  target_score_6mo: 8
```

**Total TRUST baseline (5 pillar × 0-10) feeds:**
- **Phase E Content Plan** — content gaps → sitemap inclusion
- **Phase G Growth retainer** — improvement targets per quarter
- **Client reporting** — quarterly TRUST progression as deliverable
- **EYWA Compound Growth dashboard** (Part 20 KPI integration)

## 30.8 EYWA DNAi Diagnostic — Two-Touchpoint Brand Discipline

Brand alignment is enforced at **two pipeline touchpoints** — light awareness during drafting, formal AI gate before publish. The first prevents drift early; the second catches what humans miss at scale.

### 30.8.1 Touchpoint 1 — Draft-Time Awareness (Lightweight)

**When:** From the moment content drafting starts (T-template chosen, body being written).

**Who:** Content author (operator + AI co-author).

**What's referenced:**
- `docs/brand-genesis/eywa-dna-graph.md` (10 fields — especially Brand Personality + Anti-traits + Discriminator + Compliance Boundaries)
- `strategy/messaging.md` voice ID + 5 axes (or equivalent brand voice doc)
- Brand-specific anti-patterns list

**How enforced (not blocking, instructional):**
- Content brief (per DR-017) auto-includes top-of-mind summary of voice ID + 3 anti-traits + relevant compliance line
- AI co-author (Claude Code) prompt template includes brand DNA snippet so first draft already speaks in voice
- Editorial checklist in template (per Content_Templates v1.6 §7) reminds author to cross-reference DNA Graph before submitting draft

**Goal:** **Draft enters Stage 1 review already 80-90% on-brand.** DNAi Diagnostic at Stage 2 catches the remaining 10-20% drift, not 100% rewrite work.

### 30.8.2 Touchpoint 2 — Pre-Publish Formal Gate (Serious AI Check)

**When:** After human editorial review (Stage 1), before final approval (Stage 4).

**Who:** AI (Claude API via n8n) — operator reviews output.

**What's referenced:** Same brand context as Touchpoint 1, but now applied with strict pass/fail scoring instead of authoring guidance.

**Position in editorial workflow** (extends Bible Part 23.4 multi-stage review):

```
Stage 0: Content drafting (Touchpoint 1 — brand awareness ACTIVE during writing)
   ↓
Stage 1: Human editorial review (accuracy, citations, voice — Part 23.4 existing)
   ↓
Stage 2: EYWA DNAi Diagnostic (Touchpoint 2 — formal AI brand alignment gate)  ⭐
   ↓
Stage 3: Revise if needed → re-run DNAi
   ↓
Stage 4: Final approval gate (human signoff)
   ↓
Stage 5: Publish
```

**Why two touchpoints (not just the end gate):**

- **Cost efficiency** — DNAi API calls are not free; first-pass awareness reduces revision cycles per piece
- **Author skill compounding** — writers learn the brand voice from in-flow guidance, not post-hoc rejection
- **Pipeline throughput** — fewer publish-gate failures means content velocity holds
- **Brand culture** — brand consistency becomes habit during creation, not punishment after-the-fact

**n8n workflow:**

```yaml
trigger:
  notion_page_status_change: "ready_for_dnai_check"

n8n_flow:
  step_1_pull_brand_context:
    - eywa-dna-graph.md (10 fields)
    - messaging.md OR strategy/voice (voice ID + 5 axes)
    - anti-patterns list (per brand)
    - eywa-dna-graph field 10 (Compliance Boundaries)

  step_2_claude_api_call:
    prompt: |
      "Check this content against brand DNA Graph + voice + compliance.
       Return JSON: { pass: bool, score: 0-100, issues: [{issue, severity, suggestion}],
       revised_draft: string }"
    inputs:
      - content_draft (from Notion page)
      - brand_context (compiled from step 1)

  step_3_write_back_to_notion:
    columns_updated:
      - dnai_check_status: pass | warn | fail
      - dnai_check_score: 0-100
      - dnai_check_issues: jsonb
      - dnai_check_revised_draft: text (operator review)
      - dnai_check_run_at: timestamptz

publish_gate:
  - dnai_check_status = 'pass'
  - AND human_editorial_approved (Stage 1)
  - AND final_approval_signed_off (Stage 4)
```

**Per-brand calibration:** Each brand's DNAi prompt template can be tuned by adjusting voice axes weight, severity thresholds, and compliance strictness. Stored in brand repo `deployment/dnai-config.yaml`.

## 30.11 EYWA Lexicon — Naming Definitions (do not lose meaning over time)

> **Why this section exists:** Naming locked in DR-028 follows pattern "EYWA + concept". Six months from now, operators (and AI assistants) must still know exactly what each name means, what it does, and how it differs from generic frameworks it adapts from. This section is the canonical glossary — update when meanings drift, not the names.

### 30.11.1 EYWA DNA Graph

```yaml
name: EYWA DNA Graph
adapted_from: Unilever Brand Key (10-field rubric for brand identity)
healthcare_extension: Adds field 10 (Compliance Boundaries) — YMYL discipline

meaning: |
  The structured 10-field articulation of a brand's identity, audience, promises,
  proof, personality, differentiation, and compliance constraints. "DNA Graph"
  because (a) each field encodes inheritable brand traits — like genetic code,
  and (b) the fields cross-link semantically — like a graph, not a flat checklist.
  Acts as the single source of truth that all downstream brand work references
  (content voice, design choices, editorial decisions, even legal review).

how_it_works:
  1. Produced once in Phase A.1 via 4-6 hour workshop (operator + client)
  2. Stored as docs/brand-genesis/eywa-dna-graph.md in brand repo
  3. Referenced by every Phase B-G deliverable (KW research, sitemap, content briefs)
  4. Referenced by EYWA DNAi Diagnostic during publish gate
  5. Reviewed at major Stage gates (every 6 months minimum, on brand pivot if sooner)

deliverable_owner: Operator (+ AI co-author) facilitated; client validates
review_cadence: Stage gate revalidation (typically quarterly + on brand event)
sample_output: See template/folder-skeleton/docs/brand-genesis/eywa-dna-graph.template.md

distinct_from:
  brand_concept_md: brand-concept.md was unstructured narrative — superseded by DNA Graph
  positioning_statement: Field 8 (Brand Essence) is the positioning line; DNA Graph is the full identity
  brand_voice_guide: Voice ID lives in messaging.md — referenced by but not duplicated in DNA Graph
```

### 30.11.2 EYWA Journey Map

```yaml
name: EYWA Journey Map
adapted_from: McKinsey Consumer Decision Journey (CDJ — 2009)
healthcare_extension: Patient-specific touchpoints, healthcare-appropriate stage names

meaning: |
  The 5-stage map of how a patient moves from "first awareness of need" to
  "loyal advocate" through interactions with the brand. "Journey Map" because
  it visualizes the path; "EYWA" because the touchpoint-content mapping is
  EYWA-specific (each touchpoint binds to T-templates from Part 9 and to
  alignment-map.md goals from Phase A.4).

how_it_works:
  1. Produced in Phase A.2 (part of framework-synapse.md deliverable)
  2. 5 stages: Initial Consideration → Active Evaluation → Moment of Purchase →
     Post-Purchase → Loyalty Loop
  3. Per stage: triggers + touchpoints + content needs documented
  4. Phase E sitemap audit verifies every stage has content coverage
  5. Phase F content brief (per DR-017) cites cdj_stage field on each page

deliverable_owner: Operator (informed by client patient research)
review_cadence: Annual (or on major service launch / market shift)
sample_output: See framework-synapse.template.md (section "EYWA Journey Map")

distinct_from:
  patient_journey_md: pre-DR-028 patient-journey.md (in brand-genesis predecessor) was unstructured —
    superseded by EYWA Journey Map subsection of framework-synapse.md
  user_journey: User Journey is product/UX scope; Journey Map is full lifecycle marketing scope
  funnel: A funnel is linear conversion; Journey Map includes Loyalty Loop (post-conversion)
```

### 30.11.3 EYWA Intent Roots

```yaml
name: EYWA Intent Roots
adapted_from: Jobs-to-be-Done (Christensen, 2005 — "The Innovator's Solution")
healthcare_extension: 3-tier job framing (functional + emotional + social) tailored to medical context

meaning: |
  The structured articulation of what "jobs" a patient is hiring the brand
  to do — distinguishing functional (the task), emotional (the feeling), and
  social (the identity). "Roots" because these intents are the deepest causes
  of search behavior — keywords, page visits, conversions all stem from
  these roots. Get the roots wrong → SEO drifts; get them right → content
  resonates.

how_it_works:
  1. Produced in Phase A.2 (part of framework-synapse.md deliverable)
  2. 3 tiers of jobs: functional / emotional / social
  3. Each tier: list jobs in patient's own language (verbatim where possible)
  4. Phase B keyword research uses Intent Roots to validate KW relevance
     (KW that doesn't serve any root → cut)
  5. Phase F content brief cites which Intent Root the content serves

deliverable_owner: Operator (validated by patient interviews if available)
review_cadence: Annual + on new patient persona emergence
sample_output: See framework-synapse.template.md (section "EYWA Intent Roots")

distinct_from:
  user_personas: Personas describe WHO; Intent Roots describe WHAT THEY WANT DONE
  use_cases: Use cases are product-specific; Intent Roots are patient-life-context
  keywords: KWs are surface expressions; Intent Roots are underlying causes
```

### 30.11.4 EYWA TRUST Rubric

```yaml
name: EYWA TRUST Rubric
inspired_by: Unilever SASSY (5-pillar brand desirability rubric — FMCG, proprietary)
why_not_use_SASSY: SASSY is FMCG-fit (Science/Aesthetics/Sensorials/Said-by-Others/Young) +
  Unilever trademark + Sensorials does not apply to medical service
healthcare_replacement: Built fresh — 5 pillars chosen for YMYL discipline + E-E-A-T alignment

meaning: |
  Five-pillar evaluation framework for healthcare brand maturity, used as both
  (a) baseline audit at engagement start and (b) progress tracking over time.
  TRUST acronym = Trust · Results · Understanding · Safety · Transparency.
  Each pillar 0-10. Score gaps map directly to SEO content opportunities.
  "TRUST" because it's the foundational currency of healthcare buying decisions
  — and because it doubles as Google's stated YMYL priority signal.

how_it_works:
  1. Baseline audit in Phase A.3 (3-5 hour session per brand)
  2. Per pillar: score 0-10 + evidence + gaps + content opportunity
  3. Total TRUST score = portfolio benchmark across brands
  4. Quarterly re-audit shows progression; client-facing deliverable
  5. Pillars feed into:
     - Phase E sitemap (gaps → required pages)
     - Phase F editorial workflow (per-page TRUST signals check)
     - EYWA Compound Growth dashboard (Trust over time = compounding asset)

deliverable_owner: Operator audits, client validates evidence
review_cadence: Quarterly (re-audit) + on regulatory change / major brand event
sample_output: See template/folder-skeleton/docs/brand-genesis/eywa-trust-rubric.template.md

distinct_from:
  EEAT: Google's E-E-A-T is signals framework; TRUST is brand-state evaluation
  brand_audit: Generic brand audit covers all of marketing; TRUST is healthcare-specific
  SASSY: Different domain (FMCG vs healthcare), different pillars, EYWA-owned (no IP conflict)

trademark_intent: Pursue ™ registration as EYWA proprietary methodology (Phase 2 operator action)
```

```yaml
name: EYWA Compound Growth
adapted_from: OKR framework (Doerr/Grove — outcome-based goal tracking)
```

### 30.11.6 EYWA DNAi Diagnostic

```yaml
name: EYWA DNAi Diagnostic
new_creation: Not adapted from existing framework — EYWA-original AI workflow
healthcare_metaphor: "Diagnostic" because it diagnoses brand-alignment health of content
  before publish (parallel to clinical diagnostic — find issue before treatment failure)

meaning: |
  The AI-powered brand-alignment check that runs at TWO touchpoints in the
  editorial pipeline: (1) lightweight awareness during drafting, and
  (2) formal serious gate before publish. "DNA" because it checks alignment
  against the brand's DNA Graph (Phase A.1 deliverable). "Diagnostic" because
  it doesn't auto-fix — it diagnoses issues and suggests revisions for human
  review. "EYWA" because the prompt template is calibrated per-brand using
  DNA Graph + voice ID + Compliance Boundaries.

how_it_works:
  touchpoint_1_draft_time:
    when: From the moment content drafting starts
    who: Content author (operator + AI co-author)
    enforcement: Lightweight — context injection into AI co-author prompt +
      checklist reminder
    goal: Draft enters Stage 1 review 80-90% on-brand

  touchpoint_2_pre_publish:
    when: After human editorial review (Stage 1), before final approval (Stage 4)
    who: AI (Claude API via n8n workflow)
    enforcement: Formal — pass/fail with score, revision suggestions
    goal: Catch remaining 10-20% drift; block publish if fail

  per_brand_calibration:
    config_file: brand_repo/deployment/dnai-config.yaml
    tuning: voice axes weight, severity thresholds, compliance strictness

deliverable_owner: Operator builds n8n flow (one-time), runs per-content automatically
review_cadence: Per-content automated; flow tuning quarterly
sample_output: TBD (n8n workflow build is operator action, ~6-8 hours dev one-time)

distinct_from:
  spell_check: Mechanical syntax check; DNAi is brand-semantic check
  grammarly: Grammar/style; DNAi is brand-DNA-specific
  human_editorial_review: Human catches accuracy + citations; DNAi catches
    brand voice drift + compliance violations + DNA Graph misalignment
  YMYL_review: YMYL review is medical-claim safety; DNAi is brand-alignment
    — both required, serve different purposes
```

### 30.11.7 Universal Naming Pattern — "EYWA + concept"

**Rule:** When EYWA adapts or extends an external framework AND productizes the output as a Service Suite deliverable, the output is renamed "EYWA + concept". This:

1. **Attributes IP** — EYWA-specific adaptations carry EYWA naming, not the source framework
2. **Avoids confusion** — clients won't conflate EYWA TRUST Rubric with Unilever SASSY
3. **Builds brand vocabulary** — sales conversations + content + handover docs all reference same lexicon
4. **Enables trademark path** — productized names are candidates for ™ registration

**When NOT to rename:**
- External framework cited as INPUT (e.g., Golden Circle in framework-synapse) — keep original name
- Internal technical concepts already locked in spec (e.g., Entity Genesis Protocol — EGP — not "EYWA EGP")
- Universal standards (E-E-A-T, schema.org, CWV) — keep authoritative names

**Lock list (DR-028):** 6 names listed in sections 30.11.1 through 30.11.6 above. Future additions follow this rule and are appended here.

# PART 31: Universal Brand Design System 🆕 v3.21

> **Per DR-029 (Locked 2026-05-18)** — universal per-brand design layer. Stack-agnostic specifications + W3C DTCG tokens + raw brand assets. Applies to all brand repos regardless of stack (WP+Elementor per DR-002 or Astro per DR-EYWA-MKT-005 or future stacks).
>
> **Bootstrap Kit reference:** `templates/folder-skeleton/design/` + `templates/folder-skeleton/brand-assets/`
> **Companion DR:** DR-029

## 31.1 Why a Universal Design System Exists

Brand visual identity does NOT change when implementation stack changes. The color palette of a clinic is the color palette regardless of whether the site is built with WordPress, Astro, Next.js, or hand-coded HTML.

Pre-DR-029, brand design assets lived in `theme/brand-assets/` with no formalized tokens, no W3C-standard format, no separation between specification and implementation. Each brand reinvented color palette format, typography scale, spacing system. Stack migration meant rebuilding design system from scratch.

DR-029 establishes a universal design layer that:

1. **Captures design specifications once** — tokens + brand-foundation docs live in `design/`
2. **Consumed by any stack** — WP+Elementor sync script OR Astro tailwind import OR future tooling
3. **Designer-recognized format** — W3C DTCG is industry standard; designers + tools speak it natively
4. **Future-proof** — brand can migrate stacks without losing design system

## 31.2 Folder Structure (mandatory per-brand)

```
brands/eywa-{brand}/
├── design/                       🎨 Stack-agnostic design layer (NEW per DR-029)
│   ├── README.md                 ← workflow guide
│   ├── tokens/                   📐 DTCG-compliant JSON (source of truth)
│   ├── brand-foundation/         📋 Visual identity specs (6 Markdown files)
│   ├── component-specs/          📐 Per-component design spec
│   ├── page-templates/           🗺  Page-level layout specs
│   ├── wireframes/               🗺  Hand-drawn / lo-fi sketches
│   └── references/               💡 Mood boards, inspiration
├── brand-assets/                 🖼  Raw binary sources (NEW root location per DR-029)
│   ├── logos/
│   ├── photography/
│   ├── illustrations/
│   └── icons/
└── theme/                        🚀 Stack-specific implementation
    ├── custom-css/               (WP)
    ├── elementor-templates-overrides/  (WP)
    └── (or src/ if Astro — see DR-EYWA-MKT-005)
```

**Naming note:** `theme/` preserved (not renamed to `implementation/`) — WordPress community recognizes "theme" instantly; avoids cognitive load.

## 31.3 Token File Roles

Four token files in `design/tokens/`, each with distinct purpose. All use W3C DTCG JSON format.

| File | Purpose | Update frequency |
|------|---------|------------------|
| `core.tokens.json` | Primitives — palette, type scale, spacing scale | Rare — brand identity locks |
| `semantic.tokens.json` | Role-based — primary/surface/text/border semantic mappings | Rare — semantic mappings stable |
| `component.tokens.json` | Component-level — button-bg, card-shadow, input-border | Per new component additions |
| `brand.tokens.json` | Brand-unique — pillar colors, signature accents | Brand event (pillar add, etc.) |

**Reference pattern:** semantic.tokens.json references core via `{path.to.token}` syntax. component.tokens.json references both. brand.tokens.json may reference core or stand alone.

## 31.4 DTCG Format (W3C standard)

```json
{
  "color": {
    "brand": {
      "primary": {
        "$value": "#1E40AF",
        "$type": "color",
        "$description": "Primary brand color"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Mandatory fields:** `$value` (the value), `$type` (recommended for tooling).
**Optional:** `$description` (encouraged for non-obvious tokens).
**Reference syntax:** `{path.to.token}` resolves to another token's value.

**Why DTCG over custom:**
- W3C Design Tokens Community Group spec — emerging industry standard
- Figma + Tokens Studio plugin enables 2-way sync between Figma and `design/tokens/`
- Style Dictionary transforms DTCG → CSS/SCSS/JS/Swift/Android output
- Designers recognize format on first glance — no brand-specific learning curve

## 31.5 Brand-Foundation Markdown Specs

Six markdown files in `design/brand-foundation/` document design decisions in designer-readable prose:

| File | Content |
|------|---------|
| `color-system.md` | Palette rationale + semantic mapping + WCAG contrast verification |
| `typography.md` | Typeface choices + scale rationale + voice extension + Thai/EN pairing |
| `spacing.md` | Spacing scale + layout grid + breakpoints + radius |
| `iconography.md` | Icon library + style discipline + size conventions + accessibility |
| `imagery.md` | Photography style + illustration guidelines + image specs + PDPA |
| `motion.md` | Animation principles + duration/easing tokens + `prefers-reduced-motion` |

Each .md cross-references the tokens it documents. Tokens are the machine-readable source of truth; markdown is the human-readable explanation.

## 31.6 Stack-Specific Consumption Pipelines

### WordPress + Elementor (DR-002 default stack)

```yaml
pipeline:
  1. Designer edits design/tokens/*.tokens.json
  2. Sync script transforms DTCG tokens → Elementor global colors/fonts JSON
  3. Import JSON into Elementor (Site Settings → Import Site Kit)
  4. All Elementor templates using global colors/fonts update automatically
  5. theme/custom-css/ holds tokens-derived CSS variables that Elementor globals don't cover
```

**Sync script implementation:** Operator workload (Phase 1F). Recommended: Style Dictionary with custom Elementor format transformer. ~4-6 hours one-time setup, then automated.

### Astro (DR-EYWA-MKT-005 stack profile)

```yaml
pipeline:
  1. Designer edits design/tokens/*.tokens.json
  2. tailwind.config.mjs auto-imports tokens (Style Dictionary or direct require)
  3. npm run build → CSS regenerates
  4. Astro components use Tailwind classes generated from tokens
```

### Figma 2-way sync (when designer uses Figma)

```yaml
pipeline:
  1. Tokens Studio plugin in Figma reads design/tokens/*.tokens.json via GitHub
  2. Designer changes values in Figma using Tokens Studio
  3. Tokens Studio commits back to design/tokens/ via GitHub API
  4. Stack-specific pipelines (above) pick up new values on next build
```

## 31.7 Workflow Examples

### Workflow 1 — Designer onboarding to new brand

```
1. Designer clones brand repo
2. Opens design/README.md — understands folder layout (universal pattern)
3. Reads design/brand-foundation/color-system.md — sees palette rationale
4. Opens design/tokens/core.tokens.json — recognizes DTCG format
5. Connects Figma via Tokens Studio if applicable
→ Designer productive within 1 hour, no per-brand format learning
```

### Workflow 2 — Designer changes brand primary color

```
1. Designer edits design/tokens/core.tokens.json — brand-primary.500
2. Commits + pushes
3. CI/CD triggers stack-specific pipeline (WP sync OR Astro rebuild)
4. Brand site reflects new color within build time
→ One change propagates to entire site automatically
```

### Workflow 3 — AI co-author (Claude Code) generates new component

```
1. Operator describes component need (e.g., "Hero with pillar accent")
2. Claude Code reads design/tokens/ + design/brand-foundation/ + design/component-specs/Hero.md (if exists)
3. Claude Code generates Astro/WP component referencing tokens
4. Generated component is consistent with brand by construction
→ AI-generated work matches brand discipline without per-component re-explanation
```

## 31.8 Retrofit Policy for Existing Brands

Per DR-029, existing brands (13 brand repos + eywa-marketing) retrofit at their own pace:

- **At next Stage gate** — operator creates `design/` and `brand-assets/` folders per Bootstrap Kit
- **Minimum viable retrofit** — `design/tokens/core.tokens.json` filled with at least primary palette + body typography + base spacing
- **Move existing assets** — `git mv theme/brand-assets/ brand-assets/` preserves history
- **No retroactive deadline** — Pre-Stage 1 brands can fill incrementally; brands in Phase E+ should backfill before Phase F content production starts
